NKT cells (a) are depleted from the PBMC of HIV-infected patients when compared to healthy donors; (b) the depletion is out of proportion to the loss of conventional T cells; and (c) the NKT cell depletion is most prominent during the early stage of HIV infection.
NKT cells, a subset of T cells that are activated by the lipid antigen α-galactosylceramide, are depleted from the blood of HIV-infaced patients.

NKT cells may be infected and killed by HIV early in infection, but that this does not necessarily mean that NKT cells have a role in the pathogenesis of HIV.
NKT cells appear to be a target for HIV infection, but the role of NKT cells, if any, in HIV disease progression remains to be determined.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Vα24/Vß11 NKT cell subset is depleted in HIV infection, and that depletion occurs very early after infection, and is not simply a consequence of CD4+ T cell loss.
